universe_note: Chain-level screen: every name the chain touches, built PER LINK in method section 6 priority order (money corner first, then CHOKE_POINT, then by impact). Four of twelve links are worked here: power-equipment (the money corner, 5 names), grid-interconnect, liquid-cooling and energy-generation. The eight remaining links are named in data_gaps as searched-or-not-searched rather than left silent: foundry and advanced-packaging are CHOKE_POINT links and rank above the worked non-money-corner links, but their example tickers are non-US (2330.TW, BESI.AS, ASX) or already-crowded US names, and no market or EDGAR data has been fetched for any of them, so working them now would produce rows with nothing in them. That is a coverage gap in the fetch plane, not a finding about those links. Every number on every row is read from data/market/<T>.json or computed from it; every quote is verified verbatim against data/edgar/docs/<T>.json by tools/check_screen.py.

notes.text: PCS crowdedness is reported on every row and is load-bearing for nothing. This run is the clearest evidence yet that it should not be: Axis A reads ETN, a widely-held electrical major, as DARK at 100.0 on three retail-attention fields with media null. Axis A measures RETAIL chatter, so a DARK read on a large cap is a coverage artifact, not an attention gap. method section 3 already prints PCS as ADVISORY; this row-set is why that matters.
